drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna give the added one-fifth as the reason the owner opens the bidding?
outcomeNote: The difficulty is left standing at the close of this unit and is answered in the next.

segments.he: שֶׁהַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין חוֹמֶשׁ וְכוּ׳. מַאי אִירְיָא שֶׁהַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין חוֹמֶשׁ? תִּיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּאַיְּידֵי דַּחֲבִיבָה עֲלֵיהּ טָפֵי וּפָרֵיק לַהּ! וְעוֹד, מִצְוַת גְּאוּלָּה בָּאָדוֹן!
segments.en: The mishna teaches that the one who consecrated the field opens the bidding, «as the owner gives» an additional «one-fifth» payment whereas others do not give an additional one-fifth payment. The Gemara asks: «Why» does the mishna state that the reason he opens the bidding is «specifically» because «the owner gives» an additional «one-fifth? Let» the tanna «derive» it from the reason «that since» the field «is dear to» the owner «he» would «increase» his bid «and redeem it» for a higher price. «And furthermore,» doesn’t the «mitzva of redemption» begin «with the owner» of the field by Torah law?

moves.summary: and redemption is by Torah law the owner's mitzva in the first place
moves.about: a second reason the mishna could have given: by Torah law the mitzva of redemption begins with the owner
